subject: Dedicated reserve options & ramp plan — Hyperion Labs
messages:
From: Emma Liao <emma.liao@hyperionlab.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nathan Cho <nathan.cho@hyperionlab.com>, contracts@hyperionlab.com
Date: 2028-04-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity options for upcoming pilot

Thanks again for the call this morning, Chloe — good to connect. As discussed, Hyperion is planning a four-month pilot for our Gen‑AI search and summarization workflow. High-level numbers attached (hyperion-forecast-q2.xlsx) but quick summary:

- Expected steady-state request mix: 80% embeddings/recall, 20% generation
- Peak concurrent RTGPU needs: ~30-40 vGPUs during morning ingest windows
- Average daily token load: ~120M tokens/day at pilot peak
- Target start: mid-May, with a rapid customer demo in early June

We need a short proposal that maps to: cluster size guidance, minimum guaranteed GPUs, a 3‑month ramp schedule, and an estimate of monthly burn by tier (burst vs reserved). Also want to surface any SLA or credit impacts tied to committed capacity.

Nathan (cc) is our procurement lead — he'll own contract routing. Can you send a draft that includes a simple ramp (month 1/2/3), what a conservative min GPU looks like, and what options exist to burst beyond the reserve? Ideally we get something by EOD Monday so we can prep for internal review.

Thanks —
Emma
Senior Product Ops, Hyperion Labs

----
Attachment: hyperion-forecast-q2.xlsx (xlsx spreadsheet)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@hyperionlab.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Nathan Cho <nathan.cho@hyperionlab.com>, contracts@hyperionlab.com
Date: 2028-04-01T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for upcoming pilot

Hi Emma — great meeting earlier. Thanks for the forecast file, that helped a lot. Draft attached: scaleband-proposal-v1.pdf and a GPU matrix (gpu-matrix.xlsx). High level — three pickup options we recommend based on your traffic profile:

1) Anchor 16 (Conservative)
- Cluster: 4 x A100-80GB (approx 16 worker GPUs usable for model serving)
- Min GPUs (committed): 16
- Ramp: Month1=16, Month2=24 (add 8), Month3=32 (add 8)
- Best for: tight initial spend and steady growth; allows modest burst to 1.5x with shared pool

2) ScaleBand 32 (Balanced)
- Cluster: 8 x A100-80GB (32 usable GPUs)
- Min GPUs: 32
- Ramp: Month1=24 (partial activation), Month2=32, Month3=48 (burst-enabled)
- Includes prefix cache and batching recommendations to lower token burn

3) Burst-Heavy 64 (Aggressive)
- Cluster: 16 x A100-80GB (64 usable GPUs) with reserved burst bucket
- Min GPUs: 48 (committed), burst up to 64 under credit system
- Ramp: Month1=32, Month2=48, Month3=64
- Best for: quick go‑to‑market and heavy parallelization of inference jobs

Notes / assumptions:
- Pricing tiers in attached CSVs show committed vs burst hourly rates.
- SLA: our Dedicated SLA applies to committed capacity only; burst capacity is best-effort, but we can add a formal fallback policy.
- Warmup: we recommend a 48–72 hour prewarm window before your demo to populate KV cache for your prompt distribution.

Next steps: Ben can run a short priced schedule against the forecast and flag any anomalous token assumptions. If this direction looks good, I’ll produce a V2 with explicit monthly $ impact and an outline of ramp checkpoints (usage review at weeks 2/6/10).

Would you and Nathan be available for a 30m follow-up Tuesday morning?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

----
Attachments: scaleband-proposal-v1.pdf (pdf), gpu-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Liao <emma.liao@hyperionlab.com>, Nathan Cho <nathan.cho@hyperionlab.com>, contracts@hyperionlab.com
Date: 2028-04-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve options & ramp plan — Hyperion Labs

Looping in quick pricing/activation notes (see attached price-scenarios.csv). Key clarifications from an ops/finance perspective:

- Minimums: for a production‑grade serving profile with your concurrency, 16 GPUs is a firm technical minimum; commercial minimums should be set at 24 to avoid frequent autoscale churn during peak windows.
- Recommended commit profile for pilot: Start with Commit=24 (month1), Commit=32 (month2), Commit=48 (month3). This matches the balanced ScaleBand approach but keeps short-term cost predictable.
- Burst mechanics: burst outside the committed pool is charged at the burst hourly rate; we advise a 25% burst credit bucket seeded at contract start (equivalent to ~180 extra GPU-hours) to smooth the first month.
- SLA / credits: financial credits for infra downtime apply only to committed capacity. If Hyperion requires a guaranteed burst SLA, we can discuss a custom SLA (adds a premium).

Proposed ramp checkpoints:
- Kickoff (Day 0): seed prefix cache, reserve 24 GPUs
- Week 2: operational review — KPIs: p95 latency, tokens/min, KV cache hit%
- Week 6: increase commit to 32 if KPIs stable
- Week 10: target commit 48; review contract vs. actual burn for PO adjustments

If Chloe wants, I’ll fold numbers into a short three‑page SOW appendix for Nathan/contracts to sign.

Ben
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

----
Attachment: price-scenarios.csv (csv export)

Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve options & ramp plan — Hyperion Labs

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with our internal thinking. A few clarification items before we route to procurement: 

1) If we commit to 24->48 over three months, is there a mechanism to reduce committed GPUs (down to 24) if our demo doesn't drive expected usage? Any early-exit or downscale window?
2) Can you provide a ballpark of monthly $ burn for the ScaleBand 32 commitment at 32 committed GPUs (assume token efficiency improvements reduce token cost by 12% after cache tuning)?
3) For the seeded burst credit: can you explain how that applies across regions and if it is pro-rated against a global commit?
4) We need a draft SOW and a DocuSign-ready signature bundle for Nathan/contracts by Monday.

Also, Nathan — can you confirm the billing contact and whether Hyperion will require PO or net-30?

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve options & ramp plan — Hyperion Labs

Emma / Nathan — thanks for the questions. Short answers below and I attached an updated proposal (scaleband-proposal-v2.pdf) with the dollarized burn estimates. HubSpot deal and DocuSign links are included for convenience.

1) Downscale / exit: We offer two operational windows for downscaling: a one-time 30-day grace window after Month 3 that allows a single step-down up to 50% of committed GPUs (subject to notice and a short reconfiguration fee), or a quarterly adjustment aligned to billing cycles thereafter. We can document the one-time step-down in the SOW appendix.

2) Ballpark burn (ScaleBand 32): With your forecast and an assumed 12% token efficiency gain, estimated committed spend at 32 GPUs is ~$178,000/month (includes committed capacity + seeded 180 GPU-hour burst). The attached v2 breaks this into committed, burst, and expected overage buckets.

3) Burst credit mechanics: Seeded burst credits are applied at the account level and are region-agnostic for your initial pilot geography (us-west/us-east). Credits are pro-rated across active regions by usage share.

4) SOW & signature: Attached is a DocuSign-ready SOW bundle and a short appendix listing ramp checkpoints and acceptance criteria. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/link/abc123-scaleband (also in related_links).

Proposed next steps:
- Chloe/Ben will finalize SOW appendix and send to contracts@hyperionlab.com by Friday EOD.
- Kickoff target: May 15; recommend a 48-72h prewarm window May 13–15.
- Follow-up call: Tuesday 9:30am PT to walk through the v2 and SOW checklist.

If that works, Nathan/Contracts can confirm billing cadence and we'll publish the DocuSign packet.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
